source: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999, Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
scope: Additive source records only; BONAP deferred; no photo publication, species.json, or attribution modifications

records.flora_original_name: Aster drummondii Lindl. var. texanus (E.S.Burgess) A.G.Jones

morphology.leaves: Cauline leaves ovate to cordate with broad winged petioles, blades 6–12(–15) × 3–5(–6) cm, sharp serrations; upper leaves smaller
morphology.ray: Usually dark purple to blue-lavender, rarely white

qa_notes: 1999 flora treats var. texanus; species-wide traits of modern S. drummondii require FNA check.

morphology.leaves: Stem leaves sessile, linear to oblong, usually lost before flowering; persistent branch leaves 2–3 mm × around 1 mm
morphology.ray: White short ligules, just exceeding pappus
morphology.fruit: Flattened cypsela and white hairlike pappus (historical Aster genus)

qa_notes: Species source direct; compare glandular S. oblongifolium and minute ciliate phyllary tips of S. ericoides.

morphology.habit: No reliable life-cycle distinction given beyond broad perennial Aster-group characters
morphology.leaves: Historical Mahler comparison: stem leaves elliptic to oblanceolate rather than narrowly elliptic S. praealtum
morphology.heads: Outer phyllaries 1/3–1/4 as long as inner, involucres 4–5 mm in historical key
morphology.conflict: 1999 authors note specimens may resemble S. praealtum; sources disagree whether hybrid or separate species

qa_notes: HOLD: Historical 1999 text explicitly disputes taxon; never assert hybrid parentage or species concept from this reference alone.
Current accepted S. eulae requires modern FNA/nomenclatural review.

morphology.habit: Rhizomatous perennial with early-deciduous basal and large cauline leaves
morphology.leaves: Main leaves elliptic/oblanceolate to linear-lanceolate (4–)6–15 cm × (0.5–)1–2(–3.5) cm; not auriculate-clasping
morphology.heads: White rays, rarely pink; the historical key: 20–40 rays; involucre dimensions unreported at species paragraph
morphology.phyllaries: Outer phyllaries ~1/3–2/3 as long as inner in subsp. lanceolatus; large leafy head bracts usually absent
morphology.fruit: Gray mature cypselae in comparison to brown/purple S. praealtum; historical key

qa_notes: Historical authors report intergradation/hybridization with S. praealtum; keep subspecies treatment explicit.

morphology.leaves: Numerous persistent oblong to linear-lanceolate cauline blades, often subclasping; branch leaves 3–10 × 1–2 mm
morphology.heads: Involucres 8–12 mm wide, heads relatively open/not tightly crowded

qa_notes: Distinctly glandular head stalks and phyllaries are more decisive than flower color.

morphology.leaves: Stem leaves obovate/spatulate, grayish-green and conspicuously auriculate-clasping; branch leaves smaller and appressed
morphology.heads: Showy, 20–35 mm diameter with rays spread; involucres 7–15 mm broad
morphology.rays: Blue or purple (occasionally pink/white), ligules 10–15(–17) mm
morphology.phyllaries: Tips often glandular; infraspecific phyllary dimensions/pilosity vary

historical_names: S. patens var. patentissimum (Lindl. ex DC.) G.L.Nesom
qa_notes: Historic key warns three varieties intergrade; no assignment from species-level photo.

morphology.leaves: Mid-stem sessile, linear to narrow elliptic 4–12(–15) cm × 0.3–1.5 cm, lower leaves falling early; tiny awl-shaped branch leaves
morphology.heads: Diameter ~15–20(–25) mm when rays spread; involucres ~4–8 mm high
morphology.rays: Usually bluish-white to lavender, rarely white

qa_notes: Historical flora does not find firm distinctions among purported varieties; S. eulae and S. lanceolatum difficult to distinguish in some material.

morphology.leaves: Most stem leaves falling before flowering; persistent elliptic leaves of head-bearing branches not reduced just below heads
morphology.phyllaries: Outer 1.3–2 mm wide with forward appressed whitish pubescence and no prominent marginal cilia (historic key)
morphology.heads: Involucres 7–12 mm across; rays purple/violet, occasionally pink/white

qa_notes: Compare Aster pratensis treated separately in the historic source: wider glabrous-to-slightly-hairy outer phyllaries with ciliate margins; preserve circumscription caveat.

records.flora_original_name: Aster subulatus Michx. var. ligulatus Shinners

morphology.leaves: Linear to subulate 1–10(–20) cm × 2–4(–7) mm, shrinking upward, mostly deciduous by flowering
morphology.heads: Open heads 10–12(–15) mm diameter; involucres 3–5(–7) mm high
morphology.rays: Ligules blue, purple, violet, pink or white

qa_notes: The 1999 record is specifically var. ligulatus; taxon concepts of modern S. subulatum and S. divaricatum require secondary verification before traits are propagated.

holds.name: Symphyotrichum divaricatum
holds.reason: Historical Aster subulatus var. ligulatus note mentions Aster divaricatus illegitimate name, but no direct species-level source treatment for current S. divaricatum. Requires FNA.

holds.name: Symphyotrichum eulae
holds.reason: Taxon appears as a disputed historical hybrid/difficult species; preserve partial description, no final rank or ancestry assertion.
